item.title: Mass Producing Training Data with Surprising Side Effects
item.description: Training data can have unexpected side effects on language model behavior outside the training domain: insecure code data can induce broad misalignment, and outdated bird names can induce a 19th-century persona. item.title: Beyond the principle-practice gap: Responsible AI as situated epistemic and ethical practice
item.description: Responsible AI scholarship has found that ethical principles are frequently not reflected in AI design and development. Conceptualised as a `gap' between principle and practice, this is framed as a problem of implementation, awareness or compliance, and by implication, a deficit of systems or individual behaviour. item.title: Replicability, Reproducibility, and Robustness in Political and Social Science Research with Large Language Models
item.description: This chapter addresses the central reproducibility problem of research with large language models. LLM output is probabilistic and varies across models and versions, which can have significant effects on downstream statistical results. The chapter distinguishes between replicability, reproducibility, and robustness, and proposes a probabilistic standard based on the distribution of results, not identical outputs. item.title: Route First, See Later: Enabling Vision Agents to Reason Scientifically by Separating Routing Policy from Action Spaces
item.description: Scientific image-analysis workflows require agents to select among diverse capabilities like description, detection, counting, and segmentation. This lack of auditability renders agents unreliable for high-stakes scientific automation. item.title: SpikePose: Lightweight Video Human Pose Estimation
item.description: Efficient video human pose estimation must balance localisation accuracy, motion quality, and energy cost. We present SpikePose, a lightweight video pose estimator that pairs a frame-reset, single-step spiking encoder with motion-aligned heatmap memory (MAM). The encoder supplies per-frame spatial evidence, while MAM estimates joint displacement, aligns historical heatmaps, and adaptively fuses them with current predictions. item.description: Reconstructing full flow fields from sparse sensors requires prior assumptions about unmeasured regions and physical variables.
